facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus was described in 2017 based on a single well-preserved juvenile specimen approximately 2 meters long.
facts.quote: described in 2017 by Eberhard Frey and colleagues from a single well-preserved juvenile specimen about 2 m long.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Mauriciosaurus was discovered in the summer of 2011 by workers at a quarry near Vallecillo in Nuevo León, Mexico.
facts.quote: The type and only known specimen of Mauriciosaurus was found in the summer of 2011 by workers at a laminated limestone quarry near the town of Vallecillo, in the state of Nuevo León, Mexico.

facts.statement: The specimen was formally described in 2017 by Eberhard Frey, Eric Mulder, Wolfgang Stinnesbeck, Héctor Rivera Sylva, José Padilla Gutiérrez, and Arturo González González.
facts.quote: Eberhard Frey, Eric Mulder, Wolfgang Stinnesbeck, Héctor Rivera Sylva, José Padilla Gutiérrez, and Arturo González González described the specimen in 2017

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur that lived in Mexico during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Mauriciosaurus (meaning "Mauricio [Fernández Garza's] reptile") is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mexico.

facts.statement: The presence of the ammonite Mammites nodosoides allows the specimen to be dated to the Turonian interval.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Mauriciosaurus is associated with an ammonite, Mammites nodosoides, which is present only in the Turonian interval of the Vallecillo deposits, allowing it to be dated to that age.

facts.statement: Biostratigraphic analysis dates the slab containing Mauriciosaurus to the early Turonian portion of the Agua Nueva Formation.
facts.quote: the presence of the vascoceratid ammonite Mammites nodosoides allows the slab containing Mauriciosaurus to be dated to the early Turonian portion of the plattenkalk.

facts.statement: The habitat was the bottom of a continental shelf approximately 500 km offshore in the prehistoric Gulf of Mexico.
facts.quote: The oxygen-poor deposits that Mauriciosaurus was preserved in, collectively known as the Vallecillo plattenkalk, would have represented the bottom of a continental shelf about 500 km offshore in the prehistoric Gulf of Mexico.

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus is morphologically most similar to the polycotylids Trinacromerum and Dolichorhynchops.
facts.quote: Morphologically, it is overall most similar to the polycotyline polycotylids Trinacromerum and Dolichorhynchops.

facts.statement: Distinctive features include a complex ridge pattern on the parasphenoid, narrow palate openings, a lack of coracoid perforations, and a unique arrangement of belly ribs similar to Cryptoclidus.
facts.quote: These include the sophisticated pattern of ridges on the bottom of the parasphenoid bone on its palate; the narrow openings in the palate bordered by the pterygoid bones; the lack of perforations in the surface of the coracoid; and the highly unusual arrangement of gastralia, or belly ribs, which is only otherwise seen in the non-polycotylid Cryptoclidus.

facts.statement: The animal possessed flexible trailing edges on its flippers that acted as hydrofoils and a body outline shaped by contour fat merging the torso and tail.
facts.quote: In life, each of its four flippers bore a flexible trailing edge such that they formed hydrofoils, and contour fat created a drop-like outline of the body by merging the torso and immobile tail into a single unit.

facts.statement: A heavily pigmented lining protected the animal's internal organs from UV exposure.
facts.quote: Additionally, a heavily-pigmented lining protected the organs of the body cavity from UV exposure.

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus was a short-necked plesiosaur with a drop-shaped body and a small tail.
facts.quote: Mauriciosaurus is a short-necked plesiosaur, bearing a drop-shaped body with a small tail.

facts.statement: Adult individuals of Mauriciosaurus would have reached up to twice the length of the juvenile type specimen.
facts.quote: Adult individuals would have grown up to twice the length of the type specimen.

facts.statement: Each side of the upper jaw contained at least 42 teeth, comprising 4 in the premaxilla and 32 in the maxilla.
facts.quote: Each side of the upper jaw of Mauriciosaurus contain at least 42 teeth, including 4 in the premaxilla and 32 in the maxilla.

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus is classified as a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Mauriciosaurus (meaning "Mauricio [Fernández Garza's] reptile") is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mexico.

facts.statement: Several unique features separate Mauriciosaurus from all other polycotylids, justifying its classification as a distinct genus.
facts.quote: However, several features separate Mauriciosaurus from all other polycotylids, warranting the naming of a new genus.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Mauriciosaurus have constricted outer surfaces, distinguishing them from the cylindrical vertebrae of Trinacromerum.
facts.quote: The centra of Mauriciosaurus are constricted on their outer surfaces, unlike the cylindrical centra of Trinacromerum

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Mauriciosaurus are procoelous (concave front, convex back), while the thoracic vertebrae are platycoelous (flat on both sides).
facts.quote: The cervical centra are procoelous (concave in front and convex behind), whereas the thoracic centra are platycoelous (both surfaces are flat)

facts.statement: Unlike Dolichorhynchops, the tail vertebrae of Mauriciosaurus articulated with only one haemal arch at the back end.
facts.quote: Each caudal centra only articulated with one haemal arch at its back end, as opposed to one at each end in Dolichorhynchops

facts.statement: The coracoid bone of Mauriciosaurus lacks perforations along its midline and back margin, unlike those found in Dolichorhynchops and Trinacromerum.
facts.quote: the trapezoidal coracoid of Mauriciosaurus differs from those of Dolichorhynchops and Trinacromerum in that it lacks perforations along its midline and at its back margin

facts.statement: Unlike Eopolycotylus, the coracoid of Mauriciosaurus has a smooth surface without pits or foramina.
facts.quote: Unlike Eopolycotylus, the surface of the coracoid in Mauriciosaurus is largely smooth and devoid of pits (foramina)

facts.statement: The phalanges on the third digit of Mauriciosaurus flippers have a length-to-width ratio of 1.77.
facts.quote: Across all of the flippers, the phalanges on the third digit have a length/width ratio of 1.77

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus possesses only three distal tarsals, a trait shared with other polycotylines.
facts.quote: Another trait Mauriciosaurus shares with other polcotylines is that it bears only three distal tarsals as opposed to four

facts.statement: Dark grey, rectangular structures found in the type specimen likely represent scale-like tubercles that covered the underside of Mauriciosaurus.
facts.quote: These likely represent the scale-like tubercles that would have covered the underside of the animal

facts.statement: A dark red or grey substance found at the back of the trunk and flipper bases is likely of epidermal origin, though its exact nature is unknown.
facts.quote: This substance, which is crisscrossed by a series of straight furrows that divide it into rectangular or trapezoidal segments, is of unknown, but probably epidermal, provenance

facts.statement: A grey, glossy substance forming a cone around the tail base likely represents subcutaneous fat in Mauriciosaurus.
facts.quote: a grey, glossy, amorphous substance, which forms a thick cone surrounding the base of the tail, probably represents subcutaneous fat

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus was assigned to the family Polycotylidae by Frey et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: In 2017, Mauriciosaurus was assigned to the Polycotylidae by Frey et al.

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus is classified within the subfamily Polycotylinae based on characteristics such as the length-to-width ratio of the humerus.
facts.quote: Within the Polycotylidae, Mauriciosaurus could be assigned to the clade Polycotylinae based on the length/width ratio of the humerus

facts.statement: Frey et al. diagnosed Mauriciosaurus as a new genus based on narrow interpterygoid vacuities, lack of coracoid perforations, and a specialized gastralia arrangement.
facts.quote: In addition to these characteristics, others used by Frey et al. to diagnose Mauriciosaurus as a new genus included the narrow interpterygoid vacuities, the lack of perforations in the coracoids, and the highly specialized arrangement of the gastralia

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus likely hunted small prey because it had a slender snout and small, pointed teeth.
facts.quote: Mauriciosaurus probably pursued small prey, due to its slender snout and small, pointed teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers interpret preserved soft tissue in Mauriciosaurus as a peritoneum richly pigmented by melanocytes.
facts.quote: The soft tissue structures interpreted as the peritoneum of Mauriciosaurus would have been richly pigmented by melanocytes.

facts.statement: In modern desert or high-altitude squamates, peritoneal pigmentation protects reproductive organs from solar ultraviolet radiation, a function hypothesized for Mauriciosaurus.
facts.quote: In living squamates which reside in deserts or at high altitudes, pigmentation of the peritoneum protects the body cavity against solar ultraviolet radiation, thereby preventing damage to reproductive organs.

facts.statement: Subcutaneous adipose tissue likely streamlined the body of Mauriciosaurus, similar to marine mammals.
facts.quote: Subcutaneous adipose tissue was likely responsible for streamlining the body of Mauriciosaurus, as is also seen in marine mammals.

facts.statement: Small neural spines and weak tail muscles suggest the preserved soft tissue cone on Mauriciosaurus's tail was contour fat used for stabilization, similar to fat-tailed geckos.
facts.quote: On the tail, the small neural spines, haemal arches, and transverse processes suggest the hypaxial muscles of the tail were weak; the preserved cone of soft tissue around the tail thus plausibly represents contour fat, which served to stabilize the tail while continuing the outline of the torso onto the tail in a manner not unlike fat-tailed geckos and other geckos.

facts.statement: Soft tissue preservation indicates that Mauriciosaurus's flippers were heavily muscled and had flexible skin edges.
facts.quote: As inferred from the soft tissue preserved behind the flippers, each of the flippers in Mauriciosaurus was heavily muscled and bore a flexible trailing edge made of skin.

facts.statement: The flexible skin edges on Mauriciosaurus's flippers likely formed hydrofoils to enhance locomotion, a hypothesis previously made for plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: The trailing edge allowed each flipper to form a hydrofoil that would have enhanced locomotion, as has been previously hypothesized for plesiosaurs.

facts.statement: Due to an immobile body and a neck stiffened by overlapping cervical ribs, Mauriciosaurus relied solely on its flippers for locomotion.
facts.quote: Given the immobile body and the neck stiffened by overlapping cervical ribs, the flippers would have been the only source of locomotion.

facts.statement: While the leatherback sea turtle swims at 7 km/h, Mauriciosaurus could likely swim faster by using all four limbs for locomotion.
facts.quote: D. coriacea swims at an average velocity of 7 km/h, which is consistent with estimates of the swimming speeds of Mesozoic marine reptiles; however, Mauriciosaurus would have been capable of attaining higher speeds due to involving all four limbs in locomotion.

facts.statement: Frey et al. hypothesize that thick contour fat in plesiosaurs like Mauriciosaurus explains the rarity of preserved skin in the group.
facts.quote: Frey et al. hypothesized the thick contour fat of plesiosaurs such as Mauriciosaurus may account for the scarcity of preserved skin from members of the group.

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus fell into soft, water-soaked, anoxic sediment at temperatures between 21 and 37 degrees Celsius, conditions that preserved its skin.
facts.quote: Mauriciosaurus, however, fell on its back into soft, soupy, water-soaked, and anoxic sediment of a temperature between 21 - 37 C.

facts.statement: Anoxic conditions allowed subcutaneous fat to turn into adipocere, preserving the skin on the top half of Mauriciosaurus's body.
facts.quote: These conditions allowed the subcutaneous fat to condense into adipocere instead of decaying, which preserved the skin on the top half of the body.

facts.statement: Exposed parts of Mauriciosaurus's belly decayed before burial, causing the body cavity and gastralia to collapse.
facts.quote: However, the exposed portions of the belly largely decayed prior to burial, collapsing the body cavity and gastralia.

facts.statement: Mauriciosaurus is the first known juvenile polycotylid preserved in an environment other than shallow water.
facts.quote: Mauriciosaurus is thus the first juvenile polycotylid specimen known to have not been preserved in a shallow-water environment.

facts.statement: Oxygen-poor seafloor conditions prevented scavengers from disturbing the carcass, leading to high-quality preservation and an absence of wave or current damage.
facts.quote: The oxygen-poor seafloor would have prevented carnivores, scavengers, or substrate-dwelling animals from feeding on the deposited carcasses, explaining the quality of preservation along with the absence of waves or currents.

facts.statement: The anoxic conditions at the site where Mauriciosaurus was found are partly attributed to Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 at the Cenomanian-Turonian boundary.
facts.quote: In part, the anoxic conditions can be contributed to Oceanic Anoxic Event 2, which occurred at the Cenomanian-Turonian boundary.

facts.statement: Three species of Mytiloides, including M. kossmati, M. goppelnensis, and possibly M. mytiloides, likely lived alongside Mauriciosaurus at Vallecillo.
facts.quote: Three species of Mytiloides are associated with the ammonite Mammites nodosoides at Vallecillo, and may thus have lived alongside Mauriciosaurus - namely M. kossmati, M. goppelnensis, and possibly M. mytiloides.

facts.statement: Ammonites such as Pseudaspidoceras flexuosum, Watinoceras coloradoense, and a taxon referred to Vascoceras likely coexisted with Mauriciosaurus.
facts.quote: Other ammonites that may have coincided with Mauriciosaurus included Pseudaspidoceras flexuosum, Watinoceras coloradoense, and a taxon referred to Vascoceras.

facts.statement: Fish taxa such as Paranursallia gutturosum, Goulmimichthys roberti, Tselfatia formosa, and Rhynchodercetis sp. likely lived alongside Mauriciosaurus.
facts.quote: Other vertebrates are also present throughout the Vallecillo plattenkalk, mostly consisting of fish. Taxa that may have lived alongside Mauriciosaurus, from the Mammites nodosoides - Mytiloides kossmati biozone, include the holostean Paranursallia gutturosum, the pachyrhizodontid Goulmimichthys roberti, the plethodid Tselfatia formosa, and the alepisauriform Rhynchodercetis sp.

facts.statement: Sharks including Ptychodus mortoni, Aquilolamna milarcae, and Robertichthys riograndensis, along with other fish, were found in the same deposits as Mauriciosaurus.
facts.quote: Random surveys also revealed sharks, including Ptychodus mortoni, a lamniform, and the bizarre filter-feeding shark Aquilolamna milarcae; the enchodontoid Robertichthys riograndensis; the crossognathiform Araripichthys sp.; and an indeterminate notacanthid.

facts.statement: Rare tetrapods in the Vallecillo plattenkalk include the mosasaur Vallecillosaurus, three turtles, and a tooth referred to the pliosaur Polyptychodon.
facts.quote: Tetrapods are much rarer in the Vallecillo plattenkalk, consisting of the well-preserved back half of the aigialosaurid mosasaur Vallecillosaurus bearing soft-tissue impressions, three turtles representing two taxa, and a tooth referred to the pliosaur "Polyptychodon".

facts.statement: The pliosaur Polyptychodon is now considered a nomen dubium, with some of its teeth reclassified as belonging to polycotylids.
facts.quote: However, "Polyptychodon" has more recently been considered a nomen dubium, with some of the teeth referred to the taxon being reclassified as those of polycotylids.
